Someone studies: doctor, nurse, hospital, medicine, patient. The word "health" is absent, but later they remember seeing it.

Which explanation best fits?
a: They confuse "health" with one of the presented words because the two sound similar
They remember the topic accurately but become less willing to recognize words related to that topic
They remember a presented medical word but assign it to the wrong position in the list
The general theme made "health" a plausible detail to reconstruct
I don't know
questions.k: The general theme made "health" a plausible detail to reconstruct

questions.q:
Match each finding to the concept it illustrates.

1. Groups given different labels for the same blurry drawing report seeing different things.
2. Watching a mouth say "ga" while hearing "ba" makes people hear "da."
3. After a themed word list, people falsely recall a related word that was never shown.

Which ordering of concepts matches 1, 2, 3?
a: Expectation and context; combining the senses; gist-based false memory
Combining the senses; expectation and context; gist-based false memory
Expectation and context; gist-based false memory; combining the senses
Gist-based false memory; combining the senses; expectation and context
I don't know
questions.k: Expectation and context; combining the senses; gist-based false memory
